podcast.body: Otis Redding wrote and recorded this song in Muscle Shoals in 1965. His version portrayed a man demanding deference and dignity from his partner after a long day of work and enduring life's indignities. It went top five on Billboard's R&B chart in 1965 and cracked the pop top 40. "Written by Otis Redding and recorded by him in Muscle Shoals in 1965, respect was about a man demanding deference and dignity from his partner when he gets home from work after a long day of earning a living and enduring life's indignities."

podcast.body: The original version of "Respect" by Otis Redding, released prior to Aretha Franklin's more famous cover. Redding's version was itself a top 40 hit, though it is not as widely recognized today as Franklin's reinterpretation. "his prior version was even a top 40 hit, but it's not remotely as famous today as the reboot."
